name: Current Trends in Information Technology
scope: Data management and governance: data acquisition, processing, and storage, data governance, security, privacy, and ethics, data lifecycle management, data quality, integration, and migration, master data and metadata management, and information access and retrieval. Domain-specific data management: IoT sensor and device data, streaming and pre-processing pipelines, training data curation and labelling for machine learning, privacy-preserving data analysis, electronic health records and medical imaging data, healthcare data interoperability, security logs and threat intelligence, incident response and data forensics, and secure cloud data storage. Database systems and design: database architecture and query optimisation, data modelling and schema design, relational and non-relational systems, distributed and in-memory databases, transaction processing, and information system integration. Big data platforms and analytics: Hadoop, Spark, and NoSQL ecosystems, data lakes, warehouses, and marts, distributed file systems, large-scale batch and parallel processing, and analytics pipeline design. Real-time and streaming systems: stream and complex event processing, time-series databases, low-latency query execution, real-time visualisation, and anomaly detection over data streams. Knowledge graphs and semantic technologies: ontology design and engineering, Semantic Web standards, knowledge representation and reasoning, SPARQL query processing, and semantic extraction from unstructured text, documents, and multimedia. Emerging database paradigms: quantum query algorithms and quantum-enhanced database operations, distributed ledger and immutable databases, smart contracts, and secure multi-party computation. Network architecture and management: internetworking, protocols, routing, and switching, network security and resilience, performance optimisation and scalability, software-defined networking, network virtualisation and NFV, and network management systems. Wireless and next-generation networks: 5G and 6G systems, mobile and wireless networks, IoT connectivity and LPWAN, edge and fog networking, satellite networks, content delivery and SD-WAN, and quantum networking. Programming languages and compilers: syntax and semantics, compiler and interpreter technologies, runtime environments, memory management and garbage collection, concurrency and asynchronous models, and object-oriented, functional, imperative, and logic paradigms. Software development practice: domain-specific languages, low-code and no-code platforms, AI-assisted and generative programming, serverless and microservices architectures, blockchain and quantum programming, memory safety and secure coding standards, and software vulnerability management. Artificial intelligence and intelligent systems: machine learning and deep learning methods, cognitive computing, knowledge management, automation and decision support systems, explainability and interpretability, fairness and bias mitigation, human-in-the-loop and human–computer interaction, and affective computing. Applied intelligent systems: digital transformation initiatives, smart cities and digital twins, personalised learning and educational technology, healthcare diagnostics and patient monitoring, financial fraud detection and credit scoring, supply chain and logistics optimisation, and public sector and traffic management applications. Sustainability and green IT: energy-efficient data centres, eco-friendly cloud infrastructure, sustainable IoT deployment, and carbon-aware computing. Emerging multidisciplinary trends: bioinformatics and computational biology, neurotechnology and brain–computer interfaces, precision agriculture and smart farming systems, augmented and virtual reality, metaverse ecosystems, terahertz and quantum secure communications, satellite internet and global connectivity, and the ethical and societal dimensions of emerging technology.

name: Current Trends in Signal Processing
subject_areas: Signal Processing in Healthcare and Life Sciences
scope: Digital Signal Processing: Discrete-time signals and systems, digital filters, multirate signal processing, sampling, reconstruction, spectral analysis, fast Fourier transform, digital transformations, and real-time DSP implementations. Analog and Mixed-Signal Processing: Analog filters, signal conditioning, continuous-time processing, analog front ends, mixed-signal systems, data conversion, and hybrid analog-digital signal-processing architectures. Statistical Signal Processing: Random processes, stochastic modelling, parameter estimation, detection theory, Bayesian signal processing, statistical inference, covariance analysis, and uncertainty-aware signal analysis. Adaptive Signal Processing: Adaptive filters, LMS and RLS algorithms, adaptive noise cancellation, system identification, channel equalization, echo cancellation, online learning, and self-adjusting signal-processing systems. Time-Frequency and Time-Scale Analysis: Short-time Fourier transform, wavelet transforms, Hilbert-Huang transform, spectrogram analysis, empirical mode decomposition, and non-stationary signal analysis. Image Processing and Computer Vision: Image enhancement, restoration, segmentation, compression, feature extraction, object detection, image reconstruction, pattern recognition, and computational imaging. Audio and Speech Signal Processing: Speech recognition, speech enhancement, speaker recognition, audio compression, acoustic modelling, source separation, noise suppression, music information retrieval, and audio analytics. Biomedical Signal Processing: ECG, EEG, EMG, PPG, respiratory signals, biosignal filtering, physiological monitoring, diagnostic signal analysis, wearable-health signals, and biomedical feature extraction. Multimedia Signal Processing: Image, audio and video processing, multimedia compression, multimedia analytics, content retrieval, digital watermarking, deepfake detection, multimedia forensics, and multimodal signal fusion. Communication Signal Processing: Modulation and demodulation, channel estimation, equalization, synchronization, coding, MIMO processing, OFDM, spectrum sensing, interference mitigation, and communication-receiver algorithms. Wireless and Mobile Signal Processing: 5G, 6G, cognitive radio, massive MIMO, beamforming, mmWave signal processing, wireless channel modelling, mobility-aware processing, and intelligent wireless networks. Radar and Sonar Signal Processing: Target detection, tracking, radar imaging, beamforming, Doppler processing, synthetic-aperture radar, sonar analysis, underwater acoustics, and remote-sensing applications. Optical Signal Processing: Fiber-optic signals, optical filtering, wavelength conversion, photonic signal processing, optical communication, optical computing, integrated photonics, and nonlinear optical signal processing. Sensor Signal Processing and Data Fusion: Sensor arrays, smart sensors, wireless sensor networks, sensor calibration, sensor fusion, multisensor integration, distributed sensing, wearable sensors, and edge-based signal analytics. Control-System Signal Processing: Signal analysis for control systems, state estimation, observer design, sensor feedback, control-oriented filtering, cyber-physical systems, reinforcement-learning-assisted control signals, and MIMO control applications. Machine Learning for Signal Processing: Supervised and unsupervised learning, deep learning, convolutional neural networks, transformers, representation learning, feature learning, signal classification, regression, and data-driven signal models. Generative AI and Signal Synthesis: Generative adversarial networks, diffusion models, generative signal restoration, synthetic data generation, speech synthesis, image synthesis, and learned signal reconstruction. AI-Assisted Signal Enhancement: Denoising, deblurring, super-resolution, signal restoration, artifact removal, speech enhancement, image reconstruction, and intelligent filtering. Feature Extraction and Pattern Recognition: Feature selection, dimensionality reduction, signal descriptors, statistical pattern recognition, machine-learning-based classification, anomaly detection, and dynamic feature-stream analysis. Natural Language and Text Signal Processing: Text representation, automatic summarization, transformer-based text processing, semantic analysis, information extraction, sequence modelling, and language-related signal-processing methods. Signal Processing for Cybersecurity: Intrusion detection, anomaly detection, network-traffic analysis, encrypted signal analysis, physical-layer security, multimedia forensics, and detection of manipulated signals. Signal Integrity and Transmission: Transmission lines, impedance matching, signal distortion, waveform analysis, high-speed digital signals, interconnects, crosstalk, jitter, and signal-quality assessment. Environmental and Geophysical Signal Processing: Seismic signals, atmospheric signals, oceanographic measurements, climate time series, remote-sensing data, wave measurements, and environmental monitoring. Plant and Biological Electrical Signaling: Plant electrophysiology, bioelectrical responses, long-distance electrical signaling, plant stress monitoring, biosignal sensing in agriculture, and biological electrical communication. IoT and Edge Signal Processing: IoT sensor signals, edge analytics, embedded signal processing, low-power signal processing, real-time monitoring, distributed intelligence, and intelligent connected devices. Neuromorphic Signal Processing: Event-driven processing, spiking neural networks, neuromorphic sensors, brain-inspired computation, low-power intelligent signal systems, and hardware-efficient signal processing. Quantum Signal Processing: Quantum algorithms for signal transformation, quantum sensing, quantum signal reconstruction, quantum communication signals, quantum-enhanced estimation, and emerging quantum signal-processing methods. Digital Twins and Cyber-Physical Signal Systems: Real-time signal integration, sensor-driven digital twins, predictive modelling, simulation-linked measurements, and intelligent monitoring of cyber-physical systems. Signal Processing Hardware and Embedded Systems: DSP processors, FPGAs, GPUs, ASICs, embedded signal processors, hardware accelerators, real-time architectures, and energy-efficient signal-processing implementations. Signal Processing for Autonomous Systems: Autonomous vehicles, robotics, UAVs, navigation, localization, sensor fusion, perception, obstacle detection, and real-time decision-support signals. Emerging Trends in Signal Processing: Federated signal learning, edge AI, explainable AI for signals, privacy-preserving signal processing, multimodal AI, digital twins, quantum methods, neuromorphic computing, and next-generation signal-processing architectures.

name: E-Commerce for Future & Trends
subject_areas: Supply Chain and Customer Relationship Management and Business Process
Design of the Internet Retailing Questionnaire
Data Reduction Through Identification of Factors
scope: E-commerce business models and strategy: business-to-consumer, business-to-business, and consumer-to-consumer models, platform and marketplace strategy, omnichannel and direct-to-consumer approaches, subscription and recurring revenue models, competitive dynamics in digital markets, and digital transformation of established retailers. Consumer behaviour and online decision making: purchase intention and conversion drivers, search and product evaluation behaviour, stimulus–organism–response and related behavioural frameworks, cart abandonment and return behaviour, review and rating influence, and cross-cultural differences in online buying. Trust, privacy, and security in digital commerce: trust formation and institution-based trust, assurance seals and third-party verification, perceived risk and risk mitigation, data protection and consent practice, fraud detection and prevention, and security frameworks for online marketplaces. Digital marketing and personalisation: recommendation systems and behavioural targeting, search and marketplace advertising, conversion rate optimisation and experimentation, customer segmentation and lifetime value modelling, marketing automation, and ethical boundaries of personalisation. Social commerce and community-driven retail: social platform commerce integration, influencer and creator-led selling, user-generated content and electronic word of mouth, live commerce and shoppable media, social proof mechanisms, and community and group buying models. Mobile commerce and digital payments: mobile-first commerce design, application-based commerce ecosystems, mobile wallets and contactless payment, payment gateway architecture and interoperability, buy-now-pay-later and credit models, and financial inclusion through digital payment infrastructure. FinTech and decentralised commerce: blockchain applications in transaction integrity and provenance, smart contracts for commercial agreements, decentralised finance and its commercial implications, digital currencies and tokenised assets, and regulatory treatment of emerging payment instruments. Data analytics and artificial intelligence in commerce: clickstream and behavioural data analysis, predictive analytics for demand and churn, e-commerce data warehousing and integration architecture, machine learning for pricing and assortment, conversational commerce and AI agents, and evaluation of algorithmic decision systems in retail. Supply chain and fulfilment: order fulfilment and last-mile delivery models, real-time supply chain visibility and monitoring, demand forecasting and inventory optimisation, vendor-managed inventory and supply chain coordination, warehouse automation and RFID-enabled systems, and reverse logistics and returns management. Enterprise systems and interoperability: electronic data interchange and document standardisation, enterprise resource planning integration, API-based commerce architecture, business process modelling and re-engineering for digital operations, and integration across heterogeneous commercial systems. Cross-border and regulatory dimensions: international trade facilitation and customs digitalisation, cross-border payment and taxation, comparative regulatory frameworks, consumer protection law in digital markets, platform liability and competition policy, and compliance in multi-jurisdiction operations. Sustainable and circular commerce: environmental impact of fulfilment and packaging, green supply chain design, resale, rental, and refurbishment models, carbon accounting for digital commerce, and consumer response to sustainability claims. Immersive and emerging retail technologies: augmented and virtual reality in product presentation, virtual storefronts and marketplaces, digital twins of products and stores, voice and ambient commerce interfaces, and Internet of Things applications in smart retail environments.

name: Emerging Trends in Metabolites
subject_areas: Metabolites in Drug Discovery and Development
Metabolomics in Agriculture and Food Science
scope: Metabolomics and Metabolic Profiling: Research on comprehensive analysis of metabolites in cells, tissues, biofluids, organisms, and biological systems, including targeted and untargeted metabolomics, metabolic fingerprinting, metabolic phenotyping, and pathway-level interpretation of metabolite changes. Analytical Methods in Metabolomics: Studies on mass spectrometry, nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, chromatography, capillary electrophoresis, imaging-based metabolomics, sample preparation, metabolite extraction, analytical validation, quality control, and emerging platforms for metabolite detection and quantification. Metabolomics Data Analysis and Bioinformatics: Research on metabolite identification, normalization, statistical analysis, multivariate modelling, pathway enrichment, network analysis, database development, annotation, machine learning, computational metabolomics, and integration of large-scale metabolic datasets. Clinical and Translational Metabolomics: Studies applying metabolomics to disease diagnosis, prognosis, patient stratification, therapeutic monitoring, personalized medicine, biomarker discovery, treatment response, and translation of metabolic signatures into clinical applications. Disease Metabolomics: Research on metabolic alterations associated with cancer, diabetes, cardiovascular disorders, neurological diseases, kidney and liver disorders, infectious diseases, obesity, metabolic syndrome, inflammatory conditions, and other human diseases. Nutritional Metabolomics and Metabolic Health: Studies on diet–metabolite interactions, nutritional status, dietary interventions, food intake biomarkers, obesity, insulin resistance, gut-derived metabolites, micronutrient metabolism, and the role of nutrition in metabolic health and disease. Microbiome–Metabolome Interactions: Research on microbial metabolites, host–microbiome metabolic interactions, gut microbiota, postbiotics, microbial fermentation products, metabolic signalling, dysbiosis, and the contribution of microbial metabolites to health, disease, agriculture, and environmental systems. Pharmacometabolomics and Drug Response: Studies on metabolic responses to pharmaceuticals, treatment efficacy, toxicity, drug metabolism, pharmacokinetics, adverse effects, therapeutic monitoring, and metabolomics-based approaches to precision pharmacotherapy. Plant and Agricultural Metabolomics: Research on crop metabolism, plant stress responses, plant–microbe interactions, breeding, phytochemicals, secondary metabolites, agricultural productivity, crop quality, disease resistance, and metabolomics applications in plant and agricultural sciences. Food Metabolomics and Food Quality: Studies on food composition, authentication, adulteration, processing, fermentation, nutritional quality, bioactive compounds, food safety, sensory characteristics, storage, and metabolomics-based evaluation of food products. Environmental Metabolomics: Research on metabolic responses of organisms to pollutants, toxicants, climate stress, environmental contaminants, ecological disturbances, and other environmental factors, including biomonitoring and ecological risk assessment. Microbial Metabolomics: Studies on bacterial, fungal, and other microbial metabolic pathways, secondary metabolites, antimicrobial compounds, microbial interactions, fermentation, microbial biotechnology, and metabolite-based characterization of microbial communities. Lipidomics and Specialized Metabolite Analysis: Research on lipids, fatty acids, phospholipids, sterols, sphingolipids, and other specialized metabolite classes, including their structural characterization, metabolic pathways, biological functions, and disease associations. Multi-Omics Integration and Systems Biology: Studies integrating metabolomics with genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, epigenomics, microbiomics, and other omics approaches to understand biological networks, metabolic regulation, disease mechanisms, and complex phenotypes. Biomarker Discovery and Validation: Research on identification, verification, validation, and clinical or biological interpretation of metabolite biomarkers for disease detection, prognosis, therapeutic response, environmental exposure, nutrition, and physiological status. Metabolic Pathways and Systems Metabolism: Studies on central and secondary metabolic pathways, metabolic flux, pathway regulation, cellular energy metabolism, metabolic adaptation, signalling, homeostasis, and systems-level analysis of metabolism. Emerging Technologies in Metabolomics: Research on artificial intelligence, machine learning, single-cell metabolomics, spatial metabolomics, high-resolution mass spectrometry, biosensors, automation, real-time metabolic monitoring, and other innovative technologies advancing metabolite research. Translational and Interdisciplinary Metabolomics: Research integrating metabolomics with medicine, agriculture, food science, environmental science, biotechnology, pharmacology, microbiology, and computational science where metabolite analysis forms the central scientific contribution. The revised scope reflects the journal’s stated emphasis on metabolomics methods, data analysis, bioinformatics, and applications across medicine, agriculture, environmental science, and food science.

name: Emerging Trends in Personalized Medicines
subject_areas: Discovering drug targets and incorporating them into personalized therapy
Omics-based research on illness risk, prognosis, and treatment response
Personalization of non-drug related omics-based health interventions
Morality and regulations in personalized medicine
scope: Personalized Cancer Treatment : Targeted therapeutics, small molecule–drug conjugates, receptor-mediated drug delivery, K-Ras and oncogenic signaling pathways, circulating tumor cells, tumor organoids, microfluidic tumor models, biomarker-guided oncology trials. Pharmacogenomics and Pharmacogenetics : Single nucleotide polymorphisms, copy number variation, drug-metabolizing enzymes, genotype-guided dosing, pharmacokinetic variability, prediction of therapeutic response, pharmacogenomic clinical decision support, applications in anesthesiology and pain management. Omics and Biomarkers : Genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and lipidomics, gene signatures, diagnostic, prognostic, and predictive biomarkers, quantitative proteomics and peptidomics, mass spectrometry, sample preparation, assay sensitivity and specificity, genetic testing. Bioinformatics and Data Integration : Microarray and next-generation sequencing analysis, computational diagnostics, tumor classification, statistical and machine learning, multi-omics data integration, genome-wide association studies, biostatistics, medical informatics. Drug Target Discovery and Personalized Therapy : Target identification and validation, drug–target interaction prediction, drug repositioning, pharmacotyping, nanomedicine for targeted delivery. Antibody-Related Diseases : Antinuclear and antiphospholipid antibodies, autoimmune vasculopathy, mTOR pathway signaling, therapeutic proteins, antibody-conjugated payloads, anti-drug antibodies, immunogenicity testing, immunocapture assays. Personalized Cell and Gene Therapy : Stem cells and cancer stem cell markers, regenerative medicine, gene transfer, gene therapy, growth factors in chronic wound healing, personalized vaccine development. Neurological Personalized Medicine : Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease, other neurodegenerative disorders, traumatic spinal cord injury, molecular profiling, targeted therapy, organ-on-chip models, deep brain stimulation, neuromodulation. Nutrition, Exercise, and Lifestyle : Precision nutrition, gut microbiota, nutritional assessment and surveillance, dietary patterns, physical fitness, skeletal muscle metabolism, sleep and fatigue, mobile health technology. Ethics, Regulation, and Policy : Governance, health care regulation, soft law and self-regulation, personal genomics, big data governance, disease taxonomies, public perceptions of personalized medicine, consumerization of health care. The journal publishes original research articles, reviews, case studies, and commentaries. Authors must provide the methods, data, and simulation details needed to replicate their findings. Studies that apply a uniform treatment with no stratification by patient genotype, biomarkers, or clinical profile are out of scope. The journal serves clinicians, clinical pharmacologists, geneticists, bioinformaticians, translational researchers, and bioethics and health policy specialists.

name: Emerging Trends in Symmetry
subject_areas: Symmetry in Architecture and Built Environments
Structural and Mechanical Symmetry in Engineering

scope: The journal welcomes original research articles, computational and experimental papers, systematic literature reviews, case studies, short communications, and invited editorials in the following thematic areas: Symmetry in Architecture and Built Environment Design: architectural symmetry principles and aesthetics, building facade and structural design, interior spatial organization, residential and commercial architecture, public buildings and monuments, urban planning and streetscape design, and construction methodologies incorporating symmetry. Structural and Mechanical Symmetry Engineering: structural symmetry and load distribution, mechanical systems design and optimization, vibration control through symmetry, seismic-resistant design principles, modular construction and prefabrication, composite structural analysis, and symmetrical configurations for enhanced stability and efficiency. Computational and Digital Symmetry Applications: computational modeling of symmetrical structures, CAD and Building Information Modeling (BIM) tools for symmetry design, parametric design and algorithmic generation, 3D printing and digital fabrication of symmetrical components, digital twin technologies, and simulation-based symmetry optimization. Material Science and Crystallographic Symmetry: crystal structure and symmetry groups, material property relationships to symmetry, spectroscopic analysis of symmetric materials, nanostructures and nanomaterial symmetry, molecular symmetry in chemical design, smart materials with symmetrical properties, and composite material architecture. Applied Physics and Quantum Symmetry: symmetry in quantum systems and quantum materials, symmetry principles in electromagnetism, electromagnetic antenna design and circuit symmetry, photonics and optical symmetry, sensor design leveraging symmetry, and quantum technology applications. Control Systems and Automation Using Symmetry: symmetry-based control algorithms and feedback systems, robotics and symmetric motion patterns, mechatronic system design, cyber-physical systems with symmetrical architecture, automation and process control, and machine learning applied to symmetry optimization. Sustainable Design and Environmental Applications: sustainable architecture with symmetrical principles, eco-symmetry in infrastructure planning, smart cities and symmetrical urban design, energy-efficient building design through symmetry, climate-resilient planning, and environmental system modeling using symmetry frameworks. Interdisciplinary and Emerging Symmetry Research: symmetry in art, music, and design aesthetics, philosophical and theoretical implications of symmetry, symmetry in natural and biological systems, symmetry patterns in cultural and historical contexts, and cross-disciplinary applications of symmetry principles.

name: International Journal of Analytical and Applied Chemistry
subject_areas: Kinetics and mechanisms of chemical reactions
Structure of inorganic and organic compounds
scope: Analytical methodology: chromatographic separations including HPLC, GC, and ion chromatography, mass spectrometry and hyphenated techniques, atomic and molecular spectroscopy, electroanalytical methods, sample preparation and extraction, method development and validation, calibration and quantification, and uncertainty and quality assurance in chemical measurement. Chemical sensors and biosensors: electrochemical and optical sensing platforms, enzyme- and aptamer-based recognition, gas sensing materials and mechanisms, self-assembled monolayers and electrode modification, direct electron transfer systems, and sensor performance characterisation. Electrochemistry: battery chemistry including lithium-ion and magnesium systems, insertion electrode materials, ionic liquids as electrolytes, electrochemical CO₂ reduction, corrosion and surface finishing, impedance spectroscopy, and industrial electrochemical processes. Photoelectrochemistry: photoanode and photocathode materials, photoelectrochemical water splitting and hydrogen generation, TiO₂ and hematite photocatalysis, dye-sensitised and photoelectrochemical solar cells, charge separation and transport, photocurrent transient analysis, and photocorrosion. Synthetic organic chemistry: carbon–carbon bond formation, selective and direct fluorination, continuous-flow and microreactor synthesis, biocatalytic transformations including aldolase-mediated reactions, stereochemical control, and functional polymer synthesis. Medicinal chemistry: drug design and structure–activity relationships, heterocyclic scaffolds, prodrug strategies, fluorine in drug design, natural product derivatives and semisynthesis, antimicrobial, antiviral, and anticancer agents, and mechanistic studies of biological activity. Organometallic chemistry: metal–ligand bonding and π-complexes, metal hydrides and proton transfer, homogeneous catalysis including polymerisation and alkane activation, bioorganometallic systems, porphyrinoids and macrocyclic complexes, and organometallic compatibility with redox enzymes. Reaction kinetics and mechanisms: rate law determination, isothermal and non-isothermal kinetics, advanced oxidation processes, catalytic mechanisms, transformation product identification, and computational and molecular modelling of reaction pathways. Sorption and separation processes: adsorption isotherms and kinetic modelling, activated carbon and biochar sorbents, intraparticle diffusion analysis, ion exchange and membrane separations, and thermodynamics of sorption. Structural characterisation: crystal structure determination, X-ray absorption and XANES analysis, spectroscopic structure elucidation, elemental and compositional analysis, and characterisation of polyoxometalates and mixed metal oxides.

name: International Journal of Algorithms Design and Analysis Review
scope: Algorithm design paradigms: divide and conquer, dynamic programming and memoisation, greedy strategies and matroid structure, backtracking and branch and bound, recursive formulation and problem decomposition, and comparative analysis of paradigm choice. Complexity and computability: asymptotic analysis and lower bounds, NP-completeness and hardness reductions, complexity classes and their relationships, fine-grained complexity, average-case and smoothed analysis, and impossibility results. Data structures: search trees and balanced structures, hashing schemes and collision handling, priority queues and heaps, disjoint set union and path compression, succinct and compressed structures, persistent and concurrent data structures, and amortised analysis with potential functions. Graph algorithms: shortest path, flow, and matching algorithms, connectivity and spanning structures, graph partitioning and clustering, dynamic and incremental graph algorithms, graph exploration and traversal, and algorithms on structured graph classes including interval and planar graphs. String and sequence algorithms: pattern matching and multi-pattern search, suffix arrays, trees, and construction algorithms, approximate matching and edit distance, compressed text indexing, permutation pattern matching, and sequence algorithms for computational biology. Computational geometry: convex hulls and triangulations, geometric search and range queries, quadtrees and spatial subdivision, arrangement and intersection computation, algebraic curve and surface algorithms, and geometric approximation. Randomised and approximation algorithms: randomised construction and analysis techniques, derandomisation, approximation ratio analysis and hardness of approximation, primal–dual and LP rounding methods, set cover and packing approximations, and probabilistic guarantees. Parameterized and exact algorithms: fixed-parameter tractability, kernelisation and preprocessing, treewidth and structural parameters, exact exponential algorithms, branch-and-search techniques, and parameterized hardness. Online, streaming, and sublinear algorithms: competitive analysis of online algorithms, streaming and sketching under space constraints, sublinear-time property testing, dynamic algorithms under updates, and lower bounds in restricted models. Combinatorial optimisation and mathematical programming: integer and linear programming formulations, simplex and interior point methods, cutting plane and column generation, multi-objective and stochastic programming, fuzzy and possibilistic programming, and network flow and scheduling optimisation. Metaheuristics and search-based optimisation: evolutionary and swarm-based methods, local search and iterated variants, tabu search and simulated annealing, hybrid and memetic designs, parameter control and adaptation, and rigorous benchmarking against established baselines. Parallel and distributed algorithms: work and depth analysis, parallel algorithm design for shared and distributed memory, distributed graph and consensus algorithms, communication complexity, and external memory and cache-oblivious algorithms. Algorithm engineering and experimental analysis: implementation techniques and constant-factor optimisation, experimental methodology and benchmarking practice, algorithm libraries and reusable implementations, reproducibility of algorithmic experiments, and gap analysis between theoretical and practical performance. Applied algorithms: algorithms for scheduling and logistics, routing and vehicle routing problems, resource allocation and assignment, algorithms in bioinformatics and network science, and algorithmic methods in machine learning pipelines.

name: International Journal of Cheminformatics
scope: Chemical databases and data curation: database architecture for chemical structures, curation and standardisation workflows, structure normalisation and deduplication, data quality assessment, FAIR data practices, and integration across public resources including PubChem, ChEMBL, ZINC, DrugBank, and the Protein Data Bank. Molecular representation and descriptors: line notations and structural formats, molecular fingerprints and bit-string encodings, topological and connectivity indices, three-dimensional and pharmacophoric descriptors, tautomer and protonation state handling, and descriptor selection methods. Structure search and similarity: substructure and maximum common subgraph search, similarity and diversity metrics, kernel methods for molecular comparison, scaffold analysis and scaffold hopping, clustering of chemical libraries, and retrieval effectiveness evaluation. QSAR and QSPR modelling: model construction and variable selection, applicability domain definition, internal and external validation, quantitative structure–property prediction, and mechanistic interpretation of structure–activity relationships. Machine learning and artificial intelligence for chemistry: supervised and unsupervised learning on chemical data, deep learning architectures for molecular property prediction, generative models for molecular design, active learning and reinforcement learning in chemical search, transfer learning on sparse datasets, and model interpretability. Molecular modelling and simulation: molecular mechanics and dynamics, quantum chemical and density functional calculations, conformational sampling, binding free energy estimation, protein homology modelling, and GPU-accelerated and distributed computation. Computer-aided drug design and virtual screening: structure-based and ligand-based design, molecular docking and scoring function development, pharmacophore modelling, target and off-target prediction, drug repurposing, lead identification and optimisation, and fragment-based approaches. ADMET and pharmacokinetic prediction: solubility and permeability estimation, partition coefficient calculation, metabolism and transporter prediction, toxicity and toxicokinetic modelling, physiologically based pharmacokinetic simulation, and computational alerts for liabilities. Computer-assisted synthesis and structure elucidation: retrosynthetic analysis and route prediction, reaction outcome and yield prediction, automatic reaction mechanism generation, computer-assisted structure elucidation from spectroscopic data, and reaction database construction. Chemical graph theory and algorithms: molecular topology, graph-theoretical invariants, structure enumeration and generation, canonical labelling and isomorphism, frequent subgraph mining on chemical graphs, and complexity and performance of cheminformatics algorithms. Cheminformatics infrastructure and standards: open-source toolkits and libraries, workflow and pipeline systems, data exchange formats and ontologies, reproducibility and benchmarking practices, and interoperability between chemical and biological data resources. Chemical text and patent informatics: chemical named entity recognition, structure extraction from literature and patents, patent landscaping for chemical innovation, intellectual property mining, and bibliometric analysis of chemical research.

name: International Journal of Crystalline Materials
subject_areas: Synthesis and Processing of Crystalline Materials
Simulation and Modeling of Crystalline Materials
scope: Crystal growth and nucleation: nucleation kinetics and supersaturation, growth mechanisms and growth rate control, seeding methods, epitaxial growth, solution, melt, and vapour-phase growth, growth in confined geometries, crystal habit and morphology control, and modelling of growth processes. Synthesis and processing: sol–gel and hydrothermal routes, chemical vapour deposition, atomic layer deposition, chemical solution deposition, solid-state reactions, self-assembly and templating, biomineralisation, doping strategies, and post-growth treatment including annealing, sintering, mechanical milling, and rapid solidification. Structure determination and crystallography: single-crystal and powder X-ray diffraction, neutron and electron diffraction, crystal symmetry and space group analysis, structure solution and Rietveld refinement, charge density analysis, ab initio structure determination, twinning analysis, and crystallographic databases and software. Crystal optics: birefringence and optical anisotropy, refractive index and dispersion, optical activity and rotation, double refraction, nonlinear optical crystals, polarisation behaviour, and optical characterisation of single and polycrystalline materials. Defects and microstructure: point, line, and planar defects, vacancies, interstitials, dislocations, stacking faults, grain and twin boundaries, defect formation energetics, defect engineering, and characterisation by electron and scanning probe microscopy. Mechanical and thermal behaviour: elastic modulus, yield strength, hardness, fracture toughness, plastic deformation, fatigue and creep, thermal conductivity and expansion, heat capacity, and phase stability and transformations. Electronic, magnetic, and functional properties: electrical conductivity and resistivity, dielectric response, piezoelectricity and ferroelectricity, magnetic ordering, superconductivity, thermoelectric behaviour, and structure–property relationships in functional crystals. Computational and theoretical studies: density functional theory and electronic structure calculations, molecular dynamics and Monte Carlo methods, lattice dynamics, phase-field and finite-element modelling, kinetic Monte Carlo simulation of growth and defect evolution, multiscale approaches, computational thermodynamics, and materials informatics and machine learning. Thin films, nanocrystals, and low-dimensional crystals: epitaxial and polycrystalline films, nanocrystal and quantum dot synthesis, interface and strain engineering, coatings, and size-dependent structural and physical behaviour. Applied crystalline materials: semiconductors and optoelectronic devices, photovoltaic and photonic materials, battery and energy-storage crystals, catalytic and porous frameworks, sensor materials, pharmaceutical crystals and polymorphism, biomaterials, and additively manufactured crystalline components.

name: International Journal of Composite Materials and Matrices
subject_areas: Low and high cycle fatigue damage
Strain softening and strain-rate sensitivity damage
scope: Composite Materials Design and Engineering: Research on the design, fabrication, characterization, and performance of polymer, metal, ceramic, and hybrid composite materials, including reinforcement architecture, matrix selection, interfacial behavior, and structure–property relationships. Elastic and Elastic–Plastic Behavior: Studies on elastic instability, plastic deformation, constitutive behavior, strain stiffening, anisotropy, deformation localization, surface elasticity, and elastic–plastic response in composite and matrix materials. Damage Mechanics of Composite Materials: Research on damage initiation and evolution, isotropic and anisotropic damage, matrix cracking, fiber failure, interfacial debonding, progressive damage, and multiscale descriptions of degradation in composite systems. Fatigue, Creep, and Creep–Fatigue Interaction: Studies on low- and high-cycle fatigue, creep deformation, creep-fatigue interaction, life prediction, stress relaxation, crack initiation, cyclic damage, microstructural evolution, and long-term durability of composite and matrix materials. Fracture Mechanics and Fracture Toughness: Research on brittle, ductile, and elastic–plastic fracture; crack-tip mechanics; fracture toughness; J-integral methods; probabilistic fracture; interlaminar fracture; and fracture behavior under static and dynamic loading. Crack Initiation and Propagation: Studies on crack incubation, nucleation, growth, branching, intergranular and transgranular fracture, hydrogen-assisted cracking, cavitation, porosity effects, and microstructure-dependent crack propagation in composite and matrix systems. Impact Damage and Dynamic Response: Research on impact loading, high strain-rate behavior, impact-induced cracking, delamination, fragmentation, damage tolerance, dynamic deformation, residual strength, and failure mechanisms in composite structures. Strain-Rate Sensitivity and Constitutive Modelling: Studies on strain-rate effects, dynamic strain aging, constitutive equations, thermal activation, viscous effects, void growth and coalescence, and rate-dependent mechanical behavior under dynamic loading. Damage Tolerance and Structural Integrity: Research on residual stiffness, residual strength, defect sensitivity, damage resistance, structural integrity assessment, fatigue loading, component evaluation, and methods for preventing catastrophic failure in composite structures. Crack Repair and Self-Healing Materials: Studies on crack and microcrack repair, self-healing polymers and composites, induction healing, laser-based repair, smart materials, recoverable fracture systems, cohesive-zone approaches, and techniques for extending structural service life. Fiber-Reinforced and Polymer-Matrix Composites: Research on carbon-, glass-, natural-, and hybrid-fiber composites, polymer-matrix composites, reinforcement geometry, matrix modification, delamination, interfacial mechanics, and mechanical performance under varied loading conditions. Metal-Matrix and Hybrid Composites: Studies on particle- and fiber-reinforced metal matrices, microstructural design, effective elastoplastic behavior, interfacial bonding, progressive damage, processing, and mechanical performance of advanced hybrid systems. Soft Materials, Elastomers, and Metamaterials: Research on rubber-like materials, elastomers, soft biological tissues, soft composites, metamaterials, surface instabilities, pattern transformations, viscoelastic behavior, and nonlinear deformation of compliant material systems. Surface and Interface Mechanics: Studies on surface energy, surface stress, surface strain, interface adhesion, surface elasticity, roughness, morphology, surface phase behavior, atomistic interactions, and the role of interfaces in composite performance. Micromechanics and Multiscale Modelling: Research on micromechanical models, homogenization, representative volume elements, particle distributions, interfacial debonding, scale bridging, atomistic calculations, and multiscale prediction of composite behavior. Computational Modelling and Numerical Simulation: Studies using finite element methods, XFEM, phase-field methods, discrete element methods, material point methods, smoothed-particle hydrodynamics, stochastic models, and other numerical techniques for analyzing damage, fracture, deformation, and fluid–structure interaction. Non-Destructive Evaluation and Structural Health Monitoring: Research on non-destructive testing, damage detection, vibration-based diagnostics, thermography, ultrasonic methods, imaging, signal analysis, and structural-health-monitoring techniques for identifying defects and assessing residual life. Additive Manufacturing of Composite Materials: Studies on additively manufactured composites and matrix materials, process-induced defects, residual stresses, microstructure, anisotropy, fatigue, fracture, post-processing, and mechanical performance of printed components. Experimental Mechanics and Advanced Characterization: Research using mechanical testing, microscopy, fractography, micro- and nano-indentation, digital image correlation, thermal analysis, high-speed imaging, spectroscopy, and advanced experimental methods to evaluate composite and matrix behavior. Emerging and Interdisciplinary Composite Materials Research: Research integrating composite materials with smart structures, biomaterials, nanomaterials, energy systems, aerospace engineering, automotive engineering, civil infrastructure, computational mechanics, and advanced manufacturing where composite or matrix material behavior forms the central contribution.

name: International Journal of Chemical Synthesis and Chemical Reactions
scope: Synthetic methodology: new synthetic routes and reagents, multi-step sequences, stereoselective and enantioselective methods, protecting-group strategies, one-pot and cascade reactions, and yield and selectivity optimisation. Organic synthesis: carbon–carbon and carbon–heteroatom bond formation, functional group transformations, heterocycle construction, natural product synthesis and synthetic analogues, and organometallic reagents in synthesis. Peptide synthesis: solid-phase and solution-phase strategies, coupling reagents and racemisation control, cyclic and modified peptides, peptidomimetics and peptoids, and peptide self-assembly. Electrosynthesis: electro-organic transformations, mediated and paired electrolysis, electrode materials and surface modification, electrolyte and solvent systems, and microbial electrosynthesis for CO₂ conversion. Catalysis: homogeneous, heterogeneous, and phase-transfer catalysis, supported and bimetallic catalysts, catalyst preparation and characterisation, deactivation and regeneration, and biocatalysis including enzyme immobilisation. Reaction mechanisms and kinetics: mechanistic elucidation, rate law determination, transition-state and intermediate characterisation, chemical equilibrium, computational and theoretical mechanistic studies, and isotope-labelling studies. Materials synthesis: chemical vapour deposition, atomic layer deposition, sol–gel and hydrothermal routes, nanoparticle and nanostructure synthesis, polymer and composite synthesis, and surface functionalisation chemistry. Combustion chemistry: combustion kinetics and mechanisms, catalytic combustion, fuel characterisation for gaseous, liquid, and solid fuels, soot and pollutant formation, and thermal analysis of combustion behaviour. Reactor technologies: reactor design and scale-up, continuous-flow and microreactor systems, process intensification, mixing and residence-time analysis, computational fluid dynamics applied to reacting systems, and photochemical and sonochemical reactors. Mass and energy balance: steady-state and dynamic balances, population balance modelling, mass and heat transfer in reacting systems, thermodynamic optimisation, and process simulation and validation. Green and sustainable synthesis: solvent selection and solvent-free routes, atom economy and waste minimisation, renewable and biomass-derived feedstocks, energy-efficient reaction conditions, and life-cycle considerations in synthetic route design.

Programming environments: integrated development environment architecture, language servers and incremental analysis, editor and workspace design, live and interactive programming environments, notebook and exploratory computing environments, and evaluation of environment features against developer outcomes. Development tools and automation: build and dependency management tooling, refactoring and code transformation tools, linters, formatters, and static checkers, debugging and profiling tools, AI-assisted coding and completion tools, and empirical studies of tool adoption and effectiveness. Software visualisation and animation: visualisation of program structure and execution, call graph and dependency visualisation, algorithm animation and dynamic behaviour display, visualisation of large and time-varying software data, and evaluation of visualisation techniques for comprehension. Program comprehension and human factors: how developers read, navigate, and reason about code, cognitive load in programming tasks, naming, readability, and style effects, expertise differences and developer onboarding, error and defect introduction patterns, and controlled studies of programmer behaviour. Developer productivity and workflow: measurement of productivity and its limitations, interruption and context switching in development work, code review practice and its effects, pair and collaborative programming, remote and distributed development, and team communication around code. Code quality, maintenance, and evolution: readability and maintainability metrics, code smell and anti-pattern detection, refactoring practice and its outcomes, technical debt accumulation and repayment, legacy code comprehension and modernisation, and long-term evolution of codebases. Testing and verification from a language perspective: language features that support correctness, type-driven and contract-based assurance, property-based testing, test tooling integration with language ecosystems, and static analysis built into language toolchains. Language ecosystems and package management: package registry design and dependency resolution, versioning and compatibility policy, ecosystem health and maintenance burden, library API design and evolution, and documentation practice within language communities. Domain-specific and embedded languages: design of domain-specific languages, internal DSLs and metaprogramming facilities, language workbenches, configuration and specification languages, and evaluation of DSL adoption in practice.

name: International Journal of Concrete Technology
scope: Cement chemistry and hydration: clinker composition and phase development, hydration kinetics and reaction products, microstructure formation and pore structure evolution, calorimetric and thermal analysis, and characterisation techniques including XRD, SEM, and NMR applied to cementitious systems. Supplementary cementitious materials and alternative binders: fly ash, ground granulated blast furnace slag, silica fume, metakaolin, and calcined clays, limestone calcined clay cements, alkali-activated and geopolymer binders, calcium sulfoaluminate and expansive cements, and reactivity assessment of novel binder components. Aggregates: aggregate mineralogy, grading, shape, and texture, physical and mechanical characterisation, alkali-reactivity assessment, recycled concrete and construction waste aggregates, manufactured and lightweight aggregates, and the influence of aggregate properties on concrete performance. Mix design and fresh concrete behaviour: proportioning methods and optimisation, rheology and workability, self-compacting and pumpable concretes, admixture chemistry and compatibility, setting and early-age behaviour, plastic shrinkage and bleeding, and mixing, placing, and curing practice. Mechanical behaviour of hardened concrete: compressive, tensile, and flexural strength development, elastic modulus and stress–strain response, creep and shrinkage, fracture behaviour and size effect, fatigue under cyclic loading, and behaviour under high strain rate and impact. Durability and deterioration mechanisms: chloride ingress and reinforcement corrosion, carbonation, sulfate and acid attack, alkali–silica and alkali–carbonate reaction, freeze–thaw damage and scaling, leaching and biodeterioration, permeability and transport properties, and service life modelling. Fibre-reinforced and high-performance concretes: steel, polymeric, glass, and natural fibre reinforcement, ultra-high performance concrete, engineered cementitious composites and strain-hardening behaviour, self-healing concretes, nano-modified cementitious systems, and lightweight and functional concretes. Structural behaviour of concrete members: flexural, shear, and torsional response, serviceability and crack control, behaviour of joints and connections, precast and prefabricated systems, and performance of concrete members under fire and extreme loading. Testing, monitoring, and quality control: standardised destructive and non-destructive test methods, rebound hammer, ultrasonic pulse velocity, pullout, and maturity techniques, core testing and in-situ strength assessment, embedded sensing and structural monitoring, and statistical quality control in concrete production. Production technology and digital fabrication: batching plant operation and process control, precast manufacturing, shotcrete and specialist placement methods, mass concrete and thermal control, three-dimensional printing of cementitious materials, and automation in concrete production. Repair, strengthening, and life extension: repair material selection and compatibility, surface protection and sealers, patch repair and overlays, strengthening with composites, electrochemical rehabilitation, and assessment of intervention performance. Sustainability and circularity: embodied carbon and life cycle assessment of concrete, low-clinker and carbon-reduced mixes, carbon capture and mineralisation in concrete, recycling and reuse of concrete waste, and durability-based design for extended service life.

name: International Journal of Data Structure Studies
scope: Fundamental structures and abstract data types: arrays, lists, stacks, and queues, trees and forests, sets, maps, and multisets, specification and implementation of abstract data types, and trade-off analysis between representations. Search trees and balanced structures: binary search trees and rotation-based balancing, red–black, AVL, and weight-balanced trees, B-trees, B+ trees, and multidimensional variants, splay trees and self-adjusting structures, finger search and dynamic optimality, and bulk operations on ordered structures. Hashing and dictionary structures: open addressing and chaining schemes, cuckoo, hopscotch, and robin hood hashing, perfect and minimal perfect hashing, universal and tabulation hashing families, resizing and load factor behaviour, and dictionary maintenance under insertions and deletions. Priority queues and mergeable structures: binary, binomial, and Fibonacci heaps, pairing and rank-pairing heaps, double-ended priority queues, meldable structures, and heap performance in graph algorithm contexts. Succinct, compact, and compressed structures: rank and select structures over bit vectors, succinct trees and graphs, wavelet trees, compressed suffix arrays and FM-indexes, entropy-bounded space analysis, and space–time trade-offs in practice. Text and sequence indexing: suffix trees, suffix arrays, and affix trees, construction algorithms and their complexity, self-indexing and compressed text databases, pattern matching and repeat detection structures, and indexing for genomic and large text corpora. Geometric and spatial structures: range trees and priority search trees, quadtrees, k-d trees, and R-trees, halfedge and polyhedral surface representations, spatial indexing for multidimensional queries, and kinetic data structures for moving objects. Graph representations and structures: adjacency and incidence representations, dynamic connectivity structures, compressed and streaming graph representations, structures supporting shortest path and flow computation, and representations for very large graphs. Persistent and functional data structures: partial, full, and confluent persistence, purely functional implementations and amortisation under persistence, versioned and time-travel queries, and persistence in database and file system contexts. Concurrent and parallel data structures: lock-based and lock-free designs, linearisability and correctness conditions, memory reclamation and hazard pointers, transactional memory support, contention and scalability under high core counts, and concurrent dictionaries and queues. External memory and cache-aware structures: input–output model analysis, cache-oblivious layouts and algorithms, buffer trees and write-optimised structures such as log-structured merge trees, structures for solid state and non-volatile memory, and paging and replacement behaviour. Probabilistic and approximate structures: Bloom filters, quotient filters, and variants, count-min and count sketch summaries, HyperLogLog and cardinality estimation, sampling structures for streams, and error bound analysis. Analysis of data structures: worst-case, average-case, and amortised analysis, potential function methods, lower bound techniques in the cell probe model, competitive analysis of dynamic structures, and experimental validation of theoretical bounds. Implementation and engineering: memory layout and locality optimisation, generic and library design, benchmarking methodology for structures, portability across hardware including GPU and manycore, and reusable data structure library development.

name: International Journal of Energetic Materials
subject_areas: synthesis and sensitivity of energetic materials
scope: Energetic Materials Chemistry and Design: Research on the chemistry, molecular structure, physicochemical properties, formulation principles, and performance relationships of energetic materials, with emphasis on safe scientific characterization and materials development. Propellants and Energetic Formulations: Studies on solid, liquid, hybrid, and composite propellant systems; binders, plasticizers, oxidizers, additives, compatibility, aging, mechanical behavior, and formulation stability for aerospace and industrial applications. Pyrotechnic and Reactive Materials: Research on pyrotechnic compositions, reactive materials, ignition behavior, heat generation, combustion characteristics, thermal response, and controlled energetic applications in engineering and industry. Combustion, Deflagration, and Detonation Science: Fundamental and computational studies of combustion, flame propagation, deflagration-to-detonation phenomena, shock interactions, reaction kinetics, pressure development, and energy-release mechanisms in energetic systems. Thermal Decomposition and Reaction Kinetics: Research on thermal stability, decomposition pathways, reaction mechanisms, activation energies, heat-release behavior, aging, and kinetic modeling using calorimetric and thermoanalytical methods. Sensitivity, Stability, and Safety Assessment: Studies on impact, friction, electrostatic, shock, thermal, and other sensitivity characteristics; chemical and physical stability; compatibility; hazard classification; risk assessment; and scientifically validated methods for safe handling and storage. Energetic Materials Characterization: Research using spectroscopy, microscopy, thermal analysis, diffraction, chromatography, mechanical testing, computational analysis, and related methods to characterize composition, morphology, structure, thermal behavior, and material performance. Computational Chemistry and Molecular Modeling: Studies using density functional theory, molecular dynamics, quantum chemistry, molecular orbital calculations, thermochemical modeling, and computational screening to understand energetic-material structure, stability, reactivity, and performance. Nanoenergetic and Advanced Energetic Materials: Research on nanoscale energetic systems, nanocomposites, metastable intermolecular composites, functional additives, advanced oxidizers, high-energy-density materials, and engineered microstructures with improved controllability and material performance. Thermal Protection and High-Temperature Materials: Studies on thermal protection systems, ablative materials, heat-resistant composites, refractory materials, coatings, insulation systems, and materials designed to withstand extreme thermal and reactive environments. The journal specifically identifies thermal protection materials as a core area. Energetic Material Processing and Manufacturing Science: Research on material preparation, particle engineering, mixing, granulation, coating, curing, consolidation, additive manufacturing, quality control, and process monitoring, with emphasis on reproducibility, safety, and materials performance. Ignition and Combustion Diagnostics: Studies on ignition mechanisms, flame characteristics, combustion efficiency, pressure-time behavior, spectroscopic diagnostics, high-speed imaging, thermal diagnostics, and non-invasive measurement techniques for energetic-material research. Hazard Testing and Process Safety: Research on thermal runaway, fire and explosion hazards, process-safety assessment, calorimetry, accident prevention, hazard identification, consequence analysis, and risk-management frameworks relevant to energetic materials and reactive systems. Detection and Sensing of Energetic Materials: Studies on spectroscopic, optical, electrochemical, biosensing, remote-sensing, and machine-learning-assisted approaches for the safe detection, identification, monitoring, and screening of energetic substances. Environmental Impact and Sustainable Energetic Materials: Research on environmentally preferable energetic materials, reduced-toxicity formulations, emissions, residue characterization, lifecycle considerations, waste management, environmental monitoring, remediation, and sustainable material alternatives. Aging, Reliability, and Life-Cycle Assessment: Studies on long-term stability, chemical aging, mechanical degradation, environmental exposure, storage effects, shelf-life assessment, reliability prediction, and condition monitoring of energetic materials and associated components. Energetic Materials for Aerospace and Space Applications: Research on energetic and thermal-management materials used in aerospace propulsion, launch systems, spacecraft, and related engineering environments, focusing on materials science, reliability, performance assessment, and safety. Civil and Industrial Applications of Energetic Materials: Studies on scientifically controlled uses of energetic and reactive materials in mining, construction, demolition, geotechnical engineering, materials processing, and other regulated industrial applications, with particular emphasis on safety and environmental impact. Artificial Intelligence and Data-Driven Energetic Materials Research: Research applying machine learning, artificial intelligence, cheminformatics, predictive modeling, optimization, and materials informatics to property prediction, hazard assessment, formulation screening, diagnostics, and experimental design. Emerging and Interdisciplinary Energetic Materials Research: Research integrating energetic materials with chemistry, materials science, chemical engineering, computational science, aerospace engineering, thermal science, environmental science, sensing technologies, and safety engineering where energetic-material science is the principal contribution.

Nonlinear optics, crystallography, and electronics studies with no thermal or energy application are out of scope. The journal serves mechanical and energy engineers, thermal scientists, building energy and electronics cooling specialists, researchers, and graduate students.
